absent: Locking, ordering and TLB-visibility contracts for batched PTE updates and middle or upper level installs.
Actual page sizes, shifts, masks and address-space layout values behind the boundary and size helpers.
Architecture-specific overrides for swap, unmap, cache-mode and protection transforms beyond permissive defaults.
Reverse-map walk, reference-count lifecycle and unmap traversal state machine beyond structure fields and flag values.
Huge-page install, split, collapse and reclaim mechanics beyond default unavailability reports.

findings.text: Helpers wrprotect_ptes, clear_flush_young_ptes and test_and_clear_young_ptes each handle a contiguous run of page-table slots. The first write-protects every slot in turn. The other two sample and clear the young state across the run, one with flushing semantics and one with plain test-and-clear semantics, folding all per-slot outcomes into one boolean that is true when any slot had been young. All three step the slot pointer and virtual address forward by one page per iteration until the requested count is consumed.
The default ptep_try_set helper always reports failure, meaning optimistic conditional installation of a page-table entry is unsupported and callers must fall back to another update path.

Middle-level pmdp_set_wrprotect and upper-level pudp_set_wrprotect each have two builds. One build preserves the existing entry, derives its write-protected form, and installs it for the given address space and address. The alternate build is a compile-time failure placeholder showing the operation is unavailable in that configuration.

The generic_pmdp_establish helper reads the current middle-level entry, installs the supplied replacement for the owning address space at the given address, and hands the previous value back to the caller.
Equality helpers pte_same, pmd_same, pud_same, p4d_same and pgd_same all use the same rule: two entries of one level compare equal exactly when their encoded numeric values are equal.

Permission helpers pte_access_permitted, pmd_access_permitted, pud_access_permitted, p4d_access_permitted and pgd_access_permitted share one contract: presence is always required, and a requested write additionally requires the writable attribute at that level. Reads need only presence.

Range helpers pgd_addr_end, p4d_addr_end, pud_addr_end and pmd_addr_end clamp iteration to the current block of their level. Each rounds the start up to the next block boundary of its level and returns the smaller of that boundary and the caller end, using wraparound-safe comparison near the top of the address space.

Predicates pgd_none_or_clear_bad, p4d_none_or_clear_bad, pud_none_or_clear_bad and pmd_none_or_clear_bad report true when the examined slot is empty. A slot holding a corrupt value is cleared as a side effect and also reported as empty; only a usable entry yields false. Default p4d_clear_bad and pud_clear_bad do nothing.

Protection updates use a start then commit sequence. Helpers __ptep_modify_prot_start and ptep_modify_prot_start extract the current page entry while leaving the slot non-present so hardware cannot update it concurrently. Helpers __ptep_modify_prot_commit and ptep_modify_prot_commit then install the replacement without preserving hardware state. Batched modify_prot_start_ptes merges dirty and young status from every slot of the run into its returned value, and modify_prot_commit_ptes installs uniform protection across the run while advancing the frame number slot by slot.
Defaults state that FIRST_USER_ADDRESS is zero, USER_PGTABLES_CEILING is zero, ARCH_PAGE_TABLE_SYNC_MASK is zero, and MAX_POSSIBLE_PHYSMEM_BITS is thirty two.

Modification tracking defines five bit positions __PGTBL_PGD_MODIFIED through __PGTBL_PTE_MODIFIED with values zero through four from top to page level in order, and five one-bit masks PGTBL_PGD_MODIFIED through PGTBL_PTE_MODIFIED derived from them. Mask type pgtbl_mod_mask is an unsigned integer. Enumeration pgtable_level orders PGTABLE_LEVEL_PTE then PMD then PUD then P4D then PGD from zero upward, and pgtable_level_to_str maps each to pte, pmd, pud, p4d, pgd respectively and anything else to unknown.

Leaf predicates pgd_leaf, p4d_leaf, pud_leaf and pmd_leaf default to false. Leaf sizes pgd_leaf_size, p4d_leaf_size, pud_leaf_size, pmd_leaf_size and pte_leaf_size equal the block size of their level from directory size down to single page size, and __pte_leaf_size delegates to the page size.
Helpers has_transparent_hugepage and has_transparent_pud_hugepage report only whether the corresponding transparent huge page build options were compiled in.

Limits MAX_PTRS_PER_PTE, MAX_PTRS_PER_PMD, MAX_PTRS_PER_PUD and MAX_PTRS_PER_P4D alias the configured per-table pointer counts of their level. Helper pud_pfn defaults to zero. Protection extractors pte_pgprot, pmd_pgprot and pud_pgprot default to an all-zero protection value.

Structure anon_vma holds a root pointer and a parent pointer forming a tree, a read-write semaphore, an atomic reference count, a child count, an active virtual-area count, and a cached red-black root anchoring an interval tree of related private areas.

Structure anon_vma_chain joins a virtual area pointer vma to a map pointer anon_vma. It holds a list node same_vma for area membership, a red-black node rb plus interval end rb_subtree_last for map-tree membership, with optional debug fields cached_vma_start and cached_vma_last in debug builds.

Map structure anon_vma uses its semaphore for writing during modification and for reading while walking the list. Chain field same_vma is guarded by the address-space lock together with the page-table lock, while chain field rb is guarded by the map semaphore. The tree root low bit is set only after taking that semaphore and the root must be accessed only while holding it; the bit itself is serialized by a system-wide lock used during global lock acquisition.

Unmap option enumeration ttu_flags assigns increasing single bits: TTU_USE_SHARED_ZEROPAGE the second bit, TTU_SPLIT_HUGE_PMD the third, TTU_IGNORE_MLOCK the fourth, TTU_SYNC the fifth, TTU_HWPOISON the sixth, TTU_BATCH_FLUSH the seventh, and TTU_RMAP_LOCKED the eighth.

Default hooks flush_tlb_before_set, arch_do_swap_page_nr single variant, arch_unmap_one, arch_prepare_to_swap, arch_swap_invalidate_page, arch_swap_invalidate_area, arch_swap_restore, arch_start_context_switch, arch_needs_pgtable_deposit, flush_tlb_fix_spurious_fault_pmd and init_espfix_bsp do nothing while reporting success or false need: no TLB work, no swap accounting, zero status for unmap and prepare, no invalidation or restoration, no context-switch action, no deposit need, no middle-level spurious-fault action, and no firmware fixup.

One build of arch_do_swap_page_nr fans a multi-page request out to repeated single-page arch_do_swap_page calls, stepping the address by one page per iteration and advancing both the new and old frame numbers in lockstep across the count.

Small value helpers are identity or fixed permissive defaults: move_pte returns its input entry, pte_accessible always reports accessible, pte_sw_mkyoung returns its input, pte_unused and both pte_protnone and pmd_protnone always report false, and pgprot_nx, pgprot_noncached, pgprot_mhp and pgprot_encrypted return the supplied protection unchanged while pgprot_writecombine, pgprot_writethrough and pgprot_device alias the non-cached form.

Software-dirty helpers default to inert: pte_soft_dirty and pmd_soft_dirty always report clean, while pte_mksoft_dirty, pmd_mksoft_dirty, pte_clear_soft_dirty, pmd_clear_soft_dirty, pte_swp_mksoft_dirty and both builds of pmd_swp_mksoft_dirty return the supplied entry unchanged.

Helper pgprot_modify preserves caching flavor: when the old protection matches its non-cached, combined, or device form, the same transform is reapplied to the new protection, otherwise the new protection is kept as given. Frame-map helpers pfnmap_setup_cachemode and pfnmap_track default to success without action and pfnmap_untrack does nothing, with pfnmap_setup_cachemode_pfn delegating for a single page. Helper pfn_modify_allowed defaults to allowing the change and arch_has_pfn_modify_check reports that no architecture check exists.

Several paths deliberately fail or report unavailability: pmd_write and pud_write hit a runtime failure, PAGE_NONE is a build-time failure placeholder, pmdp_collapse_flush is a build-time failure, huge helpers p4d_set_huge, pud_set_huge, pmd_set_huge, their clear forms and free helpers p4d_free_pud_page, pud_free_pmd_page and pmd_free_pte_page report zero or do nothing, one build of flush_pmd_tlb_range and flush_pud_tlb_range is a build-time failure, and the alternate pmdp_set_wrprotect and pudp_set_wrprotect builds are build-time failures.

Zero-page helpers resolve the shared zero frame in two ways: one zero_pfn build converts the per-address zero page to its frame number and the other returns a global zero frame number, while _zero_page returns the shared zero page structure for an address.

Lockless descent helpers p4d_offset_lockless, pud_offset_lockless and pmd_offset_lockless reuse the corresponding locked descent operation, passing a snapshot copy of the parent entry together with the target address.

Spurious-fault helper flush_tlb_fix_spurious_fault flushes the single faulting page. One build of flush_pmd_tlb_range and flush_pud_tlb_range delegates directly to the generic range flush for the same area and address bounds.

Helper pud_trans_unstable only inspects state when both transparent huge page support and its upper-level variant are enabled. Then it snapshots the entry and reports instability for empty, huge, or corrupt snapshots, clearing corrupt ones; in all other builds and for ordinary entries it reports stable.

Modification mask type pgtbl_mod_mask is an unsigned integer word. Level descriptor pgtable_level is an enumeration with distinct values for page, middle, upper, fourth and top levels, and pgtable_level_to_str renders each level to its short name.

Constructor DECLARE_VM_GET_PAGE_PROT provides vm_get_page_prot, which masks the supplied area flags down to read, write, execute and shared bits and indexes the global protection_map table with the result to obtain the page protection.
Kernel mappings PAGE_KERNEL_RO and PAGE_KERNEL_EXEC alias the generic kernel mapping by default. The reverse-mapping header defines guard _LINUX_RMAP_H.
